card.name: Partway through split words before s
card.fires_on: The first piece of a longer word that is cut just before an s-initial continuation, such as 'overs' in oversown, 'cons' in consisting, or the hyphen-s in -susceptible. It fires mostly in drug-label and general web text.

modes.label: Hyphen-s in susceptible
modes.description: The '-s' piece after a drug or organism name, leading into 'susceptible'.
modes.example: Rifabutin was not mutagenic in the bacterial mutation assay (Ames Test) using both rifabutin<<-s>>usceptible and resistant strains.

modes.label: Cut before s in prefixed words
modes.description: A prefix such as overs, cons or inters that is followed by the rest of the word.
modes.example: 14 ml of ciprofloxacin 0.3% and dexamethasone 0.1 % otic suspension, (<<cons>>isting of 0.42 mg

card.writes: It seems to push toward word-opening pieces like 'pre' and 'intended', which fits a word that is still being completed.
card.plain: It marks a long word broken into pieces just before an s, such as 'consisting' or 'drug-susceptible'.
